answer: Price bonds convexly in fleet size, not flat per head. The collateral required to register the k-th identity traceable to one funding source rises with k, so a lone honest agent pays only the base deposit while an operator fielding a comet-swarm of fakes faces a total bond that grows with the SQUARE of the count, not linearly. Each new clone is more expensive than the last, like claiming another dune on the same shrinking island of capital. The curve does not forbid breadth; it makes a thousand sybils cost far more than a thousand times one, so the strategy stops paying off well before scale.
